title: How the day closed
text: A mixed day. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) slipped 0.3% and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose 0.4%. NVIDIA gave back its after-hours jump from last night and closed down 3.0% at $150.86, even though its results beat expectations. Other chip makers went the other way: AMD rose 5.3% and Broadcom 3.6%. Amazon gained 3.8%. Tomorrow, watch Anthropic's first day of trading. Nothing on this page is advice; it is here to help us learn.

title: NVIDIA closed near its lowest price of the year
text: NVIDIA is now only about 1.4% above its lowest price of the past 52 weeks ($148.80) and 38% below its high. Investors seem more worried about who will lead the company than about its sales, which were strong. At least one analyst moved the stock from Buy to Hold today. The average analyst price target in our data dipped again, to about $276.

title: Fed notes point to more rate hikes
text: The Federal Reserve released notes from its October meeting. Almost all officials thought more interest rate increases would probably be needed to bring inflation back down to 2%. Many also said heavy spending on AI could push prices up. Higher rates can make borrowing more expensive and can weigh on stock prices, especially for fast-growing companies.

title: Anthropic is expected to start trading tomorrow
text: AI company Anthropic is expected to set its share price tonight and start trading on Nasdaq tomorrow under the ticker ANT. Reports say the price could land above the $70 to $78 range it first gave. Amazon, which owns part of Anthropic, rose 3.8% today. A strong or weak first day could change how people feel about AI stocks in general.

title: Not all chip stocks move together
text: On a day when NVIDIA fell 3%, AMD rose 5.3%, Broadcom 3.6% and Vertiv 2.1%. AMD had dropped more than 13% in the two days before, so part of today's gain was a bounce back. This is a good reminder that companies in the same industry can still move in different directions.

title: Lesson 57: What are Fed meeting minutes?
text: The Federal Reserve, or Fed, is the group that sets the main interest rate in the United States. About eight times a year its leaders meet to decide whether to raise, lower or hold that rate. Three weeks after each meeting, the Fed publishes the minutes: a written summary of what the leaders discussed and worried about. The decision itself is old news by then, but the minutes give clues about what the Fed might do next. That is why markets react to them. Today's minutes said almost all officials expect more rate increases. Think of it like reading the notes from a team meeting to guess the coach's next play.

title: What this covers
text: Prices, daily changes, beta and 52 week ranges for all 17 names come from the close on November 18, 2026. Analyst price targets and company ratios are available for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace; the other names show risk based on price moves only.
